title: Is FREQUENCY a comparative weight or an independent probability? The wiki calls it 'a comparative number', and E34 hinted at it: when seven suppressed species were restored, the OTHER cavern species fell 39 to 0 and 27 to 12 while an untouched control's held steady, which looks like crowding. The mix alone cannot tell the two models apart — a ratio of independent probabilities also tracks the frequency ratio — so both arms here hold the SAME 4:1 ratio at very different absolute levels: TROGLODYTE and ELK_BIRD at 100 and 25 (sum 125) against 4 and 1 (sum 5), with every other cavern-capable creature zeroed so the two compete only with each other. A season, two replicates each, tool disabled.
fork: Does total cavern arrival volume depend on the absolute frequencies, or only on their ratio — that is, can frequency be used to compose an ecosystem rather than only to switch a species off.

predictions.expects: both arms give the SAME total cavern arrivals and the same roughly 4:1 troglodyte-to-elk-bird mix; the absolute level is irrelevant and only shares matter
the same 4:1 mix in both arms, but the low arm gives far fewer total arrivals — roughly in proportion to 5 against 125
the mix does not track 4:1, and frequency is not a proportional lever at all

kill_criterion: equal totals across the two arms with a 4:1 mix in both makes frequency a comparative weight and therefore an ecosystem-composition lever; totals scaling with the absolute level makes it an independent per-species probability
culling: drop a replicate on any changed save

arms.name: high_4to1
pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.enabled=false; cfg.groups.enabled=false; cfg.ecology.enabled=false; sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.disableSched(); local z,keep=0,0; for _,cr in ipairs(df.global.world.raws.creatures.all) do if cr.underground_layer_max>=1 then if cr.creature_id=='TROGLODYTE' then cr.frequency=100; keep=keep+1 elseif cr.creature_id=='ELK_BIRD' then cr.frequency=25; keep=keep+1 else cr.frequency=0; z=z+1 end end end; print(('e35: TROGLODYTE=100 ELK_BIRD=25 (ratio 4:1, sum 125); %d other cavern-capable creatures zeroed, %d kept'):format(z,keep))

local function f(t) for _,cr in ipairs(df.global.world.raws.creatures.all) do if cr.creature_id==t then return cr.frequency end end return -1 end; local ur=df.global.world.world_data.underground_regions; local function depth(c) local r=ur[c]; return r and r.layer_depth or -1 end; local cav,deep=0,0; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do if dfhack.units.isWildlife(u) and not dfhack.units.isDead(u) and not u.flags1.inactive then local r=u.animal.population; if r.cave_id>=0 then if depth(r.cave_id)<=2 then cav=cav+1 else deep=deep+1 end end end end; local cz=0; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do if dfhack.units.isCitizen(u) and not dfhack.units.isDead(u) then cz=cz+1 end end; print(('e35: caverns=%d deep=%d citizens=%d trog_freq=%d elk_freq=%d day=%d'):format(cav,deep,cz,f('TROGLODYTE'),f('ELK_BIRD'),math.floor(df.global.cur_year_tick/1200)))
